Metadata Model: A data model or schema exists and is open-sourced;
It is machine-readable (JSON, XLSX, an API);
The metadata model connects subjects, samples and files, preserving the context needed for long-term reuse;
It states which fields are required;
The metadata model is applied in practice and verified on real-world data.
Ontologies & Vocabularies: Anatomy/tissue uses an ontology (e.g., UBERON) for cross-program comparison;
Disease/phenotype applies an ontology (e.g., DOID, MONDO, HPO) for consistent cohorts;
Assay type employs an ontology (e.g., OBI) so methods stay clear;
Terms are stored as ontology IDs, not labels, so renaming does not alter context;
Most records have terms filled in, in addition to the schema.
Persistent Identifiers: Program-assigned IDs are stable over time;
Datasets carry a DOI or registered accession;
Each release has its own versioned ID for exact citation;
Records cross-reference external databases for lasting links;
Record IDs persist across releases, so reuse stays traceable.
Overall Interoperability: A DRC-approved C2M2 submission presently hosted on the CFDE Workbench;
The submission is current, reflecting the latest data release through quarterly updates;
Submitted data files are individually listed, retrievable and verifiable (access link, checksum);
Clinical data are structured in, or mapped to, the OMOP CDM, enabling harmonized analysis with other CF Program and health system datasets;
All dataset variables and survey instruments are aligned with NIH CDEs, supporting consistent measures across CF Programs and NIH-funded studies.
Processing Provenance: Processing steps are documented for future users;
Processing code is publicly archived on a public repository;
Each data release includes the processing version used (pipeline, software or protocol);
Each output file has an execution record.
Sample Lineage: Data samples link to their source subject;
Files link to their source samples;
Links use stored IDs instead of free text;
Most of the samples from the dataset is fully linked.
Versioning: Earlier dataset release versions remain accessible;
Each dataset release version has its own persistent ID;
A version history connects all dataset releases.
Documentation: Every dataset release version has dataset release notes;
Dataset release notes explain what changed and why;
Changes are itemized by record or file.
Current Status: Data were updated in the past 12 months;
Metadata and/or code were updated in the past 12 months;
News and/or announcements were posted in the past 12 months;
Data can be accessed or downloaded.
Long-term Home: A copy is deposited in a trusted public repository;
Most of the data are preserved on an open-sourced domain;
Primary data are retained and accessible (controlled access qualifies);
Data use open, community-standard file formats;
Datasets are registered in public catalogs (e.g., dbGaP, CFDE).
Reuse & Support: A data license or data use agreement is in-place;
The data access pathway is documented;
A written data management and preservation plan exists;
Post-award support is actively pursued; community ownerships are identified;
A designated user support contact is provided.
